text: Supports PostgreSQL wire protocol, allowing any standard Postgres client driver to connect
quote: CockroachDB supports the PostgreSQL wire protocol, so you can use any available PostgreSQL client drivers to connect from various languages.

text: cockroach demo spins up a temporary in-memory cluster with an interactive SQL shell
quote: The `cockroach demo` starts a temporary, in-memory CockroachDB cluster of one or more nodes, with or without a preloaded dataset, and opens an interactive SQL shell to the cluster.

text: A single-node cluster can be run locally for quick SQL testing or app development
quote: A single-node cluster is appropriate for quick SQL testing or app development.

text: Vector indexes enable efficient approximate nearest neighbor search on high-dimensional columns
quote: A _vector index_ enables efficient approximate nearest neighbor (ANN) search on high-dimensional columns.

text: VECTOR data type is compatible with the pgvector Postgres extension
quote: `VECTOR` functionality is compatible with the [`pgvector`](https://github.com/pgvector/pgvector) extension for PostgreSQL.

text: Users can operate clusters via natural-language prompts to list tables, run statements, and insert rows
quote: A user can interact with their clusters using natural language prompts to perform read and write operations such as listing tables, executing statements, and inserting rows into a table.

text: Changefeeds stream row-level changes with at-least-once delivery and ordering guarantees
quote: CockroachDB changefeeds have an at-least-once delivery guarantee as well as message ordering guarantees.

text: Supports full and incremental backups of clusters, databases, or tables
quote: You can create full or incremental backups of a , , or . Taking regular backups of your data is an operational best practice.

text: Cluster survival goals let you configure how many simultaneous node/zone failures the database can tolerate
quote: survives** disk, machine, rack, and even datacenter failures with minimal latency disruption and no manual intervention

text: Free trial credits let you deploy a CockroachDB Standard cluster and run sample queries at no cost
quote: This page shows you how to use free trial credits to deploy a CockroachDB cluster on CockroachDB Standard and use sample code to run your first queries.

text: Provides a monthly cost estimate calculated by extrapolating current workload usage
quote: The monthly cost estimate is calculated using simple extrapolation that assumes your workload during the selected time frame is an accurate representation of your workload over the month.

text: ccloud CLI lets you create, manage, and connect to CockroachDB Cloud clusters from the command line
quote: The `ccloud` tool is a command-line interface (CLI) tool that allows you to create, manage, and connect to CockroachDB Cloud clusters.

text: Provides tooling to diagnose and optimize queries/processes consuming excessive resources
quote: Diagnose and optimize your resource consumption explains how to find and optimize queries and processes that may be consuming excessive resources.

text: Allows point-in-time restore to any moment within a backup's revision history
quote: A restore from an arbitrary point in time within the revision history of a backup.

text: Table locality settings let you control how/where table data is optimized for access, supporting low-latency geo-distribution
quote: _Table locality_ determines how CockroachDB optimizes access to a table's data.

text: ccloud quickstart command interactively creates a new CockroachDB Serverless cluster in seconds
quote: install `ccloud` and use the `ccloud quickstart` command to interactively log in and create a new CockroachDB Serverless cluster.

text: Request Unit consumption automatically scales to zero when a cluster is idle
quote: Request Unit consumption scales to zero when your cluster has no activity.

text: The Clusters dashboard page gives a high-level overview of all your clusters
quote: The **Clusters** page provides a high-level view of your clusters.
